_doc: Platform policy for the Claude MCP client lists. The HTTP set is DERIVED from cloud-infra/1_cloud-configs/dist/mcp.json (url + headersHelper); this file holds only what that derivation cannot know: endpoints reached directly rather than through the public proxy, the stdio servers that are desktop-only, and the per-platform rendering differences. Regenerate with gen-mcp-tpl.sh.

exposure._doc: BROKEN AND REVERTED 2026-09-21. Diego asked for 'the full list of MCPs with just the names exposed, then the agents query the mcp to list the tools as needed'. I implemented that by REGISTERING only cgc and moving the other nine into a _mcp_catalogue key. That does not defer tools — it DISCONNECTS the servers. A client only connects to what is in mcpServers; a url sitting in a catalogue key is never dialled, so there is no 'query it on demand' path at all. Live effect: devops_ssh_exec and devops_telegram_send stopped existing mid-conversation for the user. Every server is registered again below. The 20k ceiling is REAL and still unmet (~39,700 measured), but the fix has to be SERVER-SIDE tool reduction — collapsing cloud-infra-mcp (147 tools/17,534) and cloud-services-mcp (127/13,906) into meta-tools the way cloud-cgc-mcp went 42 -> 5, which is 31,440 of the 39,700. Client-side omission is not a budget mechanism; it is an outage.
exposure._doc_why_infra_is_not_full: cloud-infra-mcp (c3-infra) is the other PRIORITY server and is deliberately still names_only, because the measurement forbids the alternative: it alone is 147 tools / ~17,534 tokens. Registering it full leaves 2,466 tokens of the 20,000 budget, and cgc — which Diego requires to 'show it all' — needs 6,342. The two cannot both be full under the ceiling. Priority here means an agent should reach for it FIRST, not that its schemas are preloaded. Making it full again requires collapsing it to meta-tools the way cloud-cgc-mcp went 42 -> 5; until then the number decides, not the label.

measured_tokens._doc: Live tools/list payload bytes / 3.6, measured 2026-09-20. Feeds the budget guard so it is arithmetic on real numbers, not an estimate. Re-measure when a server's toolset changes; a stale entry here makes the guard confidently wrong.

exposure._doc_enforcement: 'ratchet', not 'block'. A hard fail here would refuse to generate a WORKING config in order to honour a ceiling, which is how the outage happened. The guard now reports the projected cost and fails only if it grows beyond baseline_tokens — it cannot get worse silently, and it cannot take the tools away to get better.
exposure._doc_baseline: The MEASURED total with all eleven registered (2026-09-21). Not a target — a ratchet floor. It may only ever go DOWN, and only by server-side tool reduction.

_doc_stdio_extras: EMPTY BY DESIGN (2026-09-05). This held three stdio servers that made desktop's list differ from termux's forever, which is the drift the user ruled against: 'NO MCP SHOULD BE ABSENT — THE MCP LIST MUST BE SAME EVERYWHERE'. All three are gone because the reason for each disappeared: cloud-vault-mcp and cloud-superapp-mcp were given a real StreamableHTTPServerTransport and now arrive through the DERIVED set for both platforms (verified live: POST /mcp returns 200 with serverInfo for each); cloud-cgc-pub-mcp-local ran the very same src/code/index.ts that the HTTP cloud-cgc-pub-mcp already serves, so it was a duplicate transport, not a distinct capability. Every entry also hardcoded /home/diego/... paths, which resolve on exactly one laptop and dangle everywhere else — the same machine-specific-path reason derive-mcp-json.ts skips stdio in the first place. Do NOT re-add a platform carve-out here: if a server cannot be reached over HTTP, fix the SERVICE so the deriver can see it, rather than re-splitting the lists.

termux._doc: HTTP-ONLY by decree (2026-08-08): each stdio/tsx spawn transpiles TypeScript through proot-taxed IO and cost 30s+ of claude startup.

desktop._doc: stdio DISABLED (2026-09-05) so both platforms derive from exactly the same HTTP set and the two templates are byte-identical. Termux was already HTTP-only by decree; desktop being the odd one out is what made the lists diverge. The flag is kept rather than deleted so the split is a visible, deliberate 'false' instead of a silently absent feature.

container._doc:
The my-ai_claude-api agent runner on oci-apps. It gets the SAME derived HTTP set as the two human machines — a headless agent that cannot reach the code graph reasons blind, which is exactly what a shorter list here caused. TWO declared exceptions, and no others:
  1. auth_header uses AUTHELIA_OIDC_TOKEN_CLAUDE_ADMIN with an UNDERSCORE. The container is      rendered by render-mcp.mjs, which does a literal replaceAll of that exact string at boot;      desktop and termux are rendered by nix, which substitutes the hyphenated spelling. Neither      renderer recognises the other's placeholder, so one shared spelling would silently ship an      unexpanded literal as the bearer token and 403 every gated server.
  2. output points OUT of this repository. The container image is built from a cloud-u-containers      build context that cannot reach this checkout, so its copy has to be committed there;      generating it directly is what keeps it from becoming a second hand-maintained list again.      The path is relative to ${GIT_BASE:-$HOME/git}. When that checkout is absent — cloud-infra's      lint-pipeline clones only cloud-u-linux — this platform is SKIPPED rather than failed, and      cloud-u-containers' own test-mcp-contract.sh asserts the same equality from its side.

container-goose._doc: The goose runner inside the my-ai-api container on oci-apps. Same rule as the claude       runner: a headless agent that cannot reach the code graph reasons blind. Its two servers are a      DECLARED FILTER over the shared derived set (both names must exist there or --check fails),      reached over the WireGuard mesh because goose-config.yaml carries no bearer token and the       container runs network_mode: host. format=goose-yaml renders a marked REGION inside the      committed config so the surrounding client config (providers, bundled extensions) stays       hand-authored while the server list is generated. This is a SUBSET BY DECLARATION — the      requirement cloud-c3-infra-mcp (the server the fleet keys as cloud-infra-mcp; c3-infra-mcp is      only its public URL path) and cloud-cgc-pub-mcp are present here is enforced by the filter       names themselves.
container-goose._doc_filter_removed: filter REMOVED 2026-09-21. It restricted this agent to cgc+infra while claude got eleven. Diego: 'declare ALL mcp'. A filter here is the same defect as the exposure split that just disconnected nine servers — an agent cannot call what it is not connected to, and a short list makes it reason blind (#166/#184).

container-hermes._doc: The hermes runner inside the hermes-agent container on oci-apps. Same declared filter,       same mesh transport, same region rendering as container-goose: hermes reads mcp_servers from       this file, and the gateway must keep offering cloud-cgc-pub-mcp + cloud-infra-mcp (the fleet's      canonical key for the c3-infra-mcp server). platform_toolsets must not name either server in an      allowlist or the other silently drops — the cloud-u-containers test-mcp-contract.sh asserts       that too.
container-hermes._doc_filter_removed: filter REMOVED 2026-09-21. It restricted this agent to cgc+infra while claude got eleven. Diego: 'declare ALL mcp'. A filter here is the same defect as the exposure split that just disconnected nine servers — an agent cannot call what it is not connected to, and a short list makes it reason blind (#166/#184).

_doc_auth_header: The DEFAULT placeholder written into every proxy-hosted entry. A platform may override it, because the placeholder is not read by Claude Code alone — whoever renders the template has to recognise the exact string. Nix substitutes it on desktop and termux; the container has its own renderer with its own convention.
